text:
Carla: Quick check — for per-route quotas when a client hits a burst and we return 429, what exact header set are we shipping? Also: do we want the body to include bucket id + next-available timestamp?
Ben: Plan we discussed: include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (unix ts), Retry-After (seconds). Add X-Quota-Bucket for route grouping. Body should have human-friendly reason + bucket id for debugging.
Priya: Are we sure Retry-After (seconds) is OK for SDKs in other languages? Some SDKs currently expect a unix ts in X-RateLimit-Reset.
Hafeez: We should support both patterns for backcompat: keep X-RateLimit-Reset as unix ts and Retry-After as seconds. SDKs can prefer one. Avoid changing semantics of X-RateLimit-Reset.
Mike: +1. Also note per-route burst behavior: we allow a short grace window (default 10s) where tokens can overshoot then catch up. Should we expose that in headers (e.g., X-RateLimit-Grace) or keep internal?
Ben: I'd avoid exposing grace unless we need customers to tune. Exposing too many headers encourages brittle clients. For now, X-Quota-Bucket + Reset + Remaining is enough.
Carla: For canary behavior — if Dedicated routes fallback to a cheaper model during capacity pressure, do we signal that via headers or body? We sometimes want to tell customers "degraded" so they can decide.
Priya: Maybe a small header: X-Model-Fallback: true/false or X-Model-Variant: <id>. Low overhead.
Hafeez: Implementation detail: our limiter uses a leaky token bucket per bucket id. That means Remaining can briefly go negative during allowed bursts (we clamp to 0 in headers). We should document that nuance so customers don't rely on negative values.
SRE-Bot: deploy 1864508000: rate-limiter v2 rolled to staging, includes X-Quota-Bucket header and Retry-After behavior. :rocket:
Mike: Code snippet for the response we agreed on:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1864508060
X-Quota-Bucket: write-heavy-42
Retry-After: 20
X-Model-Variant: gpt-medium-fallback
Content-Type: application/json

{ "error": "quota_exceeded", "bucket": "write-heavy-42", "next_retry_ts": 1864508060 }
```
Priya: Small ask: include a short machine-readable error code in body (we have "quota_exceeded" above) plus optional human message. That helps automated backoffs.
Carla: One more: when per-route quotas are aggregated into organization-level buckets, do we surface the org bucket id? Debugging user issues will be painful without it.
Ben: We can set X-Org-Quota-Bucket when applicable. Might be omitted for single-route buckets.
Hafeez: Edge case: clients that retry immediately on 429 can cause hot loops. We must ensure our SDKs implement jittered exponential backoff and prefer Retry-After when present.
Mike: I'll add tests to sdk-js to obey Retry-After and fall back to exponential backoff if missing.
SRE-Bot: note: open PR #498 for rate-limiter header docs + examples. Please review this week.
Carla: Thanks — tagging @Ben @Priya for follow-ups. If no objections, let's land header contract and add examples to the API docs and SDK tests.
Ben: No objections. I'll update the API contract doc and add the header matrix + a small note about grace window behavior.
Priya: I'll update SDK tests and a note in changelog. :+1:
